newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police hold suspect in serial killer case.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police hold suspect in serial killer case.

text.p: Belgian police have arrested a man in their investigations into a serial killer who has terrorised the city of Mons for the past month by dumping bin-bags containing the severed body parts of up to six women.
"A suspect in the bin-bag case was arrested at the beginning of this week," Didier Vanreusel, spokesman for the Mons public prosecutor, told Reuters by telephone on Friday.
He added that in the interest of the investigation, the arrest had been kept secret until now.
The suspect, a Belgian male who lived on the fringe of society, knew the only victim who has so far been identified, Vanreusel said.
On Wednesday, police said they had identified one of the victims as Nathalie Godart, a 21-year-old homeless Belgian girl, who was often seen hanging around the Mons railway station.

The killer, suspected of having local historical knowledge and a possible religious bent, has left about 30 body parts -- hands, feet, arms, thighs, a head and a torso -- in 15 bin-bags at four separate locations around the southern Belgian city.
Each location has had evocative names such as Street of Worry, Deposit Street and River Hate.
One street was named after Saint Symphorien, a third-century French saint who was decapitated and whose bones are kept as a relic in a nearby church.
Police say they see no link between the bin-bag serial killer case and the paedophile sex, kidnap and murder scandals that have rocked the country in the past nine months.
